title: Temporary Residential Furniture Rental and Welcome Kit Services � U.S. Embassy Bern
description: The U.S. Embassy in Bern, Switzerland invites qualified vendors to participate in a solicitation for temporary residential furniture rental and welcome kit services for government?leased residences in Bern and the surrounding areas. The selected contractor will provide a full range of services, including the delivery, installation, maintenance, and removal of residential furniture, as well as the provision of welcome kit packages for incoming U.S. Government personnel. All furnishings must be new or in excellent condition, and all mattresses must be new. The contractor must be able to respond quickly to requests, manage multiple simultaneous orders, and comply with all applicable local safety, labor, and insurance regulations. Prior experience supporting diplomatic missions or corporate housing providers is highly desirable. Interested vendors must be duly licensed to operate in Switzerland and demonstrate proven experience in residential furniture rental and logistics. The ability to provide comprehensive, end?to?end support (delivery, installation, maintenance, and removal) is essential. Vendors interested in this opportunity are invited to submit their proposals electronically to BernGSOContracting@state.gov. Complete offers must be submitted no later than 22 September 2026, 17:00 local time (Central European Time). Only technically acceptable offers will be considered for price evaluation. The contract may be awarded to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offer. The Embassy reserves the right to request clarifications or additional information during the evaluation process.

title: Open Geospatial Consortium Membership Services
description: The Office of Procurement Operations (OPO) on behalf of the Office of Science and Technology (S&T) Directorate hereby issues this notice of intent to restrict competition to Open Geospatial Consortium 2300 Wilson Blvd, Suite 700-1026, Arlington, VA 22201 for Open Geospatial Consortium Membership Services. This notice of intent to solicit and award a purchase order under the statutory authority permitting restricting competition is 41 U.S.C. 1901 implemented by Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) FAR 12.201-1, Simplified procedures. The relevant NAICS code is 519290 � Web Search Portals and All Other Information Services, with a size standard of 1,000 employees. The PSC code is R605 � Support-Administrative: Library. Summary of the Requirement Scope DHS S&T Requirements, Engineering & Acquisition (REA) requires membership to Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) an international standards organization that develops open standards for geospatial data, services, and interoperability. Office of Requirements, Engineering & Acquisition (REA) and Mission Engineering & Standards Division (MES) received requests from individuals in the Technology Center to participate in OGC. Membership in this group provides support to and participation in the development of standards that are required by Department of Homeland Security components. OGC is a standard development organization focused on geospatial and location-based information that are critical information requirements for Homeland Security and Emergency Management missions. DHS also needs to vote in critical Geospatial Standards so that its mission needs can be covered. OGC standards support interoperability by making maps, imagery, features, metadata, and services compatible without needing custom integrations. OGC standards help ensure that maps, imagery, features, metadata, and services can be shared without custom one-off integrations. Period of Performance: 12-month base period and two (2) 12-month option periods. DHS has determined that Open Geospatial Consortium membership, can only be obtained from Open Geospatial Consortium. This notice is not request for competitive quotations and is for informational purposes only. A Request for Quote is not available for this requirement. However, any information received will be considered by the Government on future acquisitions. Responses or information pertaining to this notice may be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer Donna.Wright@hq.dhs.gov by September 22, 2026, by 11:00 AM Eastern Daylight Time. Questions by phone will not be considered. A determination by the Government to restrict competition is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Automated Liquid Handling Platform
description: All equipment shall be newly manufactured. It shall not be used, refurbished, reconditioned, remanufactured, or previously used for demonstration. Salient characteristics and any single-source need The equipment shall meet the following salient characteristics: a benchtop automated liquid handling platform, user-friendly and easy to operate and clean, of space-saving and energy-saving design, capable of fast automatic pipetting of multiple solutions and of serial dilutions across or down the plate; able to accommodate variable liquid volumes; able to pipette into single rows, single columns, or individual wells as selected by the user in a 96-well or 384-well format, with the well format interchangeable based on user requirements; customizable to the laboratory's assay needs; equipped with programmable operating temperatures permitting use across a range of temperatures; and usable within the containment enclosure identified in the minimum technical requirements below to permit handling of sterile or hazardous materials. Based on our research, only a specific make and model meets our needs, the Agilent Technologies Bravo Automated Liquid Handling Platform. It is the only equipment in its class that can meet our minimum needs as listed in the specifications. Other machines do not dispense low volumes, are much larger than this machine and do not fit within a biosafety cabinet. The equipment shall meet the following minimum requirements: The platform shall be benchtop in format and shall fit and operate within a biosafety cabinet of dimensions of 46in W X 24in D X 30in H that will support 120 lbs without disrupting the enclosure airflow. The platform shall perform serial dilutions either across the plate or down the plate using standard disposable tip heads. The platform shall use 96-channel or 384-channel pipetting heads that are interchangeable, with independent tip pickup capability. The platform shall provide a minimum 15-position deck capacity. The platform shall dispense from 0.1 to 200 microliters. Dispensing accuracy and precision shall be no worse than 5% deviation. The platform shall be configurable to support shaking, heating, cooling, and filtration. These configurations are not required to be delivered with the platform; however, the platform shall be capable of accepting these configurations at a later date, if desired. The platform shall include a controller and software to generate custom protocols. The platform shall include a dedicated computer to control the machine. The platform shall be compatible with standard format microplates (96-well and 384-well). The platform shall operate under ambient conditions of 5 to 40 degrees Celsius and 10 to 90 percent relative humidity, non-condensing. No deck or plate temperature-control range is required. Compliance with all applicable Federal, state, and local safety standards.

title: Strengthening Carbon Market Readiness and Article 6 Operationalisation in Cameroon
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the Government of Cameroon. Cameroon, situated within the Congo Basin and home to significant forest carbon resources, is seeking to strengthen its readiness to participate in high-integrity international carbon markets, including Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), and voluntary carbon markets. While the country has considerable potential to generate climate finance through carbon markets and support implementation of its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), key legal, institutional, and operational gaps continue to constrain effective participation. This assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to support the Government of Cameroon in establishing the governance frameworks, institutional arrangements, and regulatory systems required to operationalise carbon market participation. Working closely with relevant government institutions, including the Ministry of Environment, Nature Protection and Sustainable Development (MINEPDED), the Ministry of Forestry and Wildlife (MINFOF), the Ministry of Finance (MINFI), and other key stakeholders, the project will strengthen carbon market governance, Article 6 implementation readiness, project approval systems, and institutional coordination mechanisms. Key outputs are expected to include a comprehensive carbon market readiness assessment, a carbon market governance framework defining the roles and responsibilities of key institutions, operational procedures for Article 6 participation and Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs), a national carbon project approval system, and a structured capacity-building programme for government counterparts. The project will also support the integration of gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) considerations, safeguarding measures, and benefit-sharing approaches within carbon market governance arrangements. The project aims to strengthen Cameroon's ability to participate credibly and effectively in international carbon markets, mobilise climate finance, enhance institutional capacity, create an enabling environment for private sector investment, and support the delivery of national climate and sustainable development objectives. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk.

title: Bangladesh Carbon Market Governance & Readiness Sprint
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the government of Bangladesh. Bangladesh is establishing the foundations for participation in high-integrity carbon markets, including Article 6, CORSIA and voluntary carbon markets. While progress has been made through the establishment of a carbon market framework and supporting governance arrangements, further support is needed to operationalise these systems across government, strengthen institutional coordination, and enable Bangladesh to use carbon markets to support delivery of its NDC 3.0 unconditional mitigation targets. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to strengthen Bangladesh's carbon market governance, authorisation processes, MRV, reporting and institutional readiness. Working with relevant government agencies, including MoEFCC, DoE, the Power Division, Ministry of Finance and other line ministries, the project will support practical implementation of carbon market rules, CORSIA readiness, UNFCCC reporting requirements, and inclusive, high-integrity market participation. Key outputs are expected to include governance and coordination tools, an authorisation and safeguards toolkit, CORSIA readiness and reporting support, a structured government capacity-building programme, and sector readiness briefs identifying future carbon market investment opportunities. The project aims to strengthen Bangladesh's ability to participate in high-integrity carbon markets, unlock climate finance, improve institutional capability, and support implementation of national climate targets. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk

title: BJS-Law Enforcement Calls for Service Data Platform
description: BJS-LAW ENFORCEMENT CALLS FOR SERVICE DATA PLATFORM This Request for Information (RFI) Notice is issued for market research purposes only and is not a solicitation for proposals. See the attached RFI for additional information. The U.S. Department of Justice/ Office of Justice Programs/ Bureau of Justice Statistics (USDOJ/ OJP/ BJS) is exploring the development of a national measure of law enforcement workload and activity that includes criminal and non-criminal police-public engagement. The concept of a national law enforcement calls for service (CFS) data platform is to establish a uniform, publicly available, event-based collection of law enforcement CFS captured in computer-aided dispatch (CAD) systems. BJS is seeking to understand the technical solutions that can automate the retrieval and standardization of information captured in CAD and can transform that information into an analyzable data system with uniform data elements and values. This Request for Information (RFI) Notice is issued for market research purposes only and is not a solicitation for proposals. --SEE THE ATTACHED RFI FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION.--

CASTLE KEEP is a customer-facing portal that provides automated workflow services and Sensitive Compartmented Army SCI program reporting, metrics, analysis, and information sharing within the Army SCI community in accordance with DoDM 5105.21 requirements. This is non-personal services contract to provide Software Development and Software Sustainment Support of the Department of Army (DA) SSO�s CASTLE KEEP. The intent of the RFI is to identify parties having an interest in bidding on and the resources to support solicitations for G2�s CASTLE KEEP�s sustainable solution for the SSO/SSR community to develop and sustain CASTLE KEEP in Army Commercial Cloud Solutions Provider (AC2SP). The Government retains ownership to software and application tools; upon completion this contract all information will be turned over to the U.S. Government and is U.S. Government property. The identified questions are to encourage competition and exchanges of information. Any voluntary response received will be reviewed to assist the Government in arriving at the most suitable approach. The Government is seeking responses to this RFI that describes vendors� existing capabilities. Small Business Participation: This RFI is issued on an unrestricted basis (Full and Open) to maximize industry responses. The Government highly encourages submissions from all business sizes and socioeconomic categories (e.g., Small Business, SDVOSB, 8(a), WOSB, HUBZone). Infrastructure Assessment: Vendor shall simulate the realistic threat exploitation techniques within the legacy, existing, and emerging software system's cybersecurity in the mission context of the representative operating environment. Vendor shall apply the cybersecurity testing process with blue teams of Government and Vendor equivalent organizations and red teams of the certified Government and Vendor equivalent organizations during Developmental/Operational Test & Evaluation (D/O T&E).The Blue team assesses the operational network vulnerability with findings for the independent technical review of the network security posture and implements the mitigation techniques for integration into the community security solution to increase the cybersecurity readiness posture. The Blue teams evaluate the security threats/risks in the operating environment and study the network environment and its current state of security readiness. The Red teams simulate the potential adversary's exploitation capabilities against an enterprise's security posture to enhance the enterprise IA/Cybersecurity via demonstration of the impacts of the successful attacks and the needed countermeasure by the blue teams in the operational environment. Cyber Integration: Vendor shall coordinate with Government Agencies and industry partners to support interoperability and integration of other capabilities, maintain adequate certified personnel to meet requirements, and provide qualified staff for CASTLE KEEP software development and sustainment. Vendor shall lease workspace with NIPRNet and JWICS access to support three to four personnel. Multi-level Security: Vendor personnel performing work under this action must have an active Top Secret (TS) security clearance with eligibility for obtaining Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) (SI, TK, G, and HCS security clearance IAW DoD 5200.1-R at the time of award and must maintain the level of security required for the life of a contract. This action will require TSI/SCI, but future work related to this action may require a TS/SCI with Counterintelligence Polygraph (TS/SCI w/CI Poly) clearance. The security requirements are IAW the attached DD Form 254, Security Classification Specification. Personnel must perform within the security limitations of AR 381-10, USSID 18, and other security regulations. Any vendor personnel that will need access to SIPRNet terminals will require a TS/SCI clearance because all SIPRNet terminals are in Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIFs) Security Boundary Clarification: The vendor shall understand and apply all applicable security classification guidance. Users should notify the originator if information indicates a need to update the guidance. Classification determinations remain the responsibility of the Government Contracting Agency (GCA). The Contract Security Classification Specification (DD254) is required for performance on a classified contract. Infrastructure for Cyber Operations: The vendor shall leverage infrastructure as code such as terraform or related for deployments and cloud management. Cyber-Network Architecture: develop, maintain, and update documentation which includes Standard Operating Procedures, System Architecture Guides, Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), Install Guides, and Department of Defense Architectural Framework (DoDAF) diagrams for all related system and hardware configurations adhering to organizational templated and policies quarterly. The vendor shall leverage cross-domain solutions for implementation for tempest hardening and significant equipment installations. The vendor shall not implement solutions that have licenses or incur additional costs without written approval from the Government stakeholders, COR, and ACOR. Post-RFI Events: Following the evaluation of RFI responses, the Government anticipates hosting an Industry Day to facilitate open exchanges of information and provide further program details. A separate announcement containing registration, scheduling, and security clearance instructions for the Industry Day will be published on SAM.gov. The feasibility of conducting associated physical site visits is currently under evaluation and will be announced at a later date, if applicable. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Vendors may only submit one (1) submission per CAGE code. Interested sources are requested to submit a response of no more than five (5) pages, written in Times New Roman font of 12-point size or larger. Times New Roman of 10-point size is acceptable for graphics, tables, or exhibits. Responses must be in either Microsoft Word or character recognized and searchable Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). If your company has different business sectors which hold different CAGE codes, each sector may submit a response. In addition, each CAGE code must provide separate facility clearance documentation which will not count against the 5 page limit. If teaming, use the Prime Vendor's CAGE code in the response. Submission of proprietary and other sensitive information must be marked and identified with disposition instructions. The Government shall not be liable or suffer any consequential damage for any improperly identified proprietary information. Proprietary information will be safeguarded in accordance with the applicable Government regulations and requirements. title: Platform One Solutions Marketplace (P1SM)/Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO)
description: Platform One, with support from its marketplace manager, The Applied Research Institute (ARI), is initiating a long-term, open call for solutions to support the DoD in quickly delivering high-quality, secure software with accelerated delivery times. The solutions will support or enable the delivery of resilient software capability at the speed of relevance, ensuring the DoD remains agile and responsive to emerging threats and opportunities. Specifically, Platform One seeks to obtain innovative solutions or potential capabilities that fulfill requirements, close capability gaps, or provide potential technological advancements. Innovative solutions encompass technologies, processes, or methods (including research and development) that are newly developed or applied in a novel way as of the submission date. This initiative, entitled the �Platform One Solutions Marketplace� (P1SM) will solicit, collect, assess, and curate hardware, software, or service solutions and make those solutions available through rapid acquisition pathways. This approach aims to foster innovation and expedite the integration of cutting-edge technologies into the DoD's operational framework, enhancing its ability to deliver software at the speed of relevance.

title: Giant Voice Replacement
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The 87th Communications Squadron (CS) Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Jersey is procuring a new requirement to engineer, Design, Furnish, Install, and Test (EDFI&T) a turnkey Giant Voice (GV) System at Joint-Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst, New Jersey (JB-MDL NJ). The current GV system consists of forty-two (42) outdoor GV poles (i.e., towers) that span over three joint base areas: McGuire, Dix, Ranges, and Lakehurst. This project will require installation of Giant Voice equipment for interoperability and compatibility with the AtHoc alert system and achieve uniformity for the whole JB-MDL GV system. The new GV system shall provide emergency messages, intelligible voice, tones, and pre-recorded alert notifications for the specified critical locations on JB-MDL NJ. It shall be able to communicate over the existing Radio Frequency (RF) communications infrastructure. The new stand-alone GV system shall provide sufficient intelligible voice coverage with real-time emergency alerting messages and accurate system health activities. Please see attached SOO for more information. Questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist, Noah Whiting at Noah.Whiting.1@us.af.mil, and the Contracting Officer, Lizbette Zalybniuk, at Lizbette.Zalybniuk.1@us.af.mil no later than 11 September 2026. ***PLEASE NOTE: There will be a site-visit associated with this requirement. The site visit will be held on location at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst on 9 September 2026 at 1000. Please contact Contract Administrator, Noah Whiting, at Noah.whiting.1@us.af.mil to be added to our EAL by the deadline of 1400 on 02 September 2026. Please note that all individuals on EAL and planning to enter JB MDL will undergo a background check. Admittance to Government Facilities will depend on the outcome of the same.***

title: Lieutenant Colonel Lionel A. Jackson (LTC LAJ) Condensers Replacement
description: Background: The Virgin Islands Army National Guard (VIARNG) utilizes heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems to support operational readiness, occupant comfort and equipment protection across multiple buildings and facilities. The current project is initiated to replace the inoperable condensing units and restore environmentally controlled air to the facility. The condensing units at the LTC Lionel A. Jackson (LTC LAJ) Readiness Center were installed several years ago and have fallen into disrepair. The systems must be replaced in order to provide a climate-controlled environment for soldiers, government employees, and other visiting personnel of the facility. Scope: The contractor shall furnish all materials, tools, supplies, equipment, labor, and professional supervision required to replace the existing condensing units and conduct servicing of the existing air handling units at the LTC LAJ Readiness Center. The sizes and manufacturers of the existing condensers to be replaced are listed on the Exhibit (Exhibit 1). The facility is located at the Estate Bethlehem Military Compound (EBMC) on the island of St. Croix, U.S. Virgin Islands.

title: Test Pit and Soil Borings
description: INTRODUCTION: Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Department of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe) is providing support to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Targeted Brownfields Assessments (TBA) Program. As part of this effort, a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) that includes a requirement for the advancement of test pits and soil borings will be conducted at the Royal Electric Yard (the Site) located at 7512 Main St, Sykesville, Maryland 21784. A 2026 Phase I ESA conducted at the Site identified historic automotive junking activities and small, partially buried piles of automotive debris in the northern, wooded portion of the property. It was determined that there is a likely presence of hazardous substances or petroleum products associated with former automotive operations including used oils, brake and hydraulic fluids, gasoline and diesel fuels, mercury switches, asbestos brake parts, refrigerants, metals, batteries, and antifreezes. A Phase II ESA was recommended to determine if these historical activities have impacted the Site. As part of this Phase II ESA, test pits and soil borings will be collected to assess any impacts from potential contaminants of concern. The property is an approximately 4.1-acre parcel (Maryland Tax Account Number #05- 072190) located adjacent to Sykesville�s historic main street district. Sykesville is located within Carroll County. Major features at the property include a warehouse, gravel parking lot, and access road in the southern portion, and an unmaintained wooded area in the northern portion. Due to a pending sale of the Site, the primary area of interest is limited to the northern half of the property. The site generally slopes to the south, with the wooded area alternating between relatively flat terraces and steeper slopes. A review of the Natural Resources Conservation Service National Cooperative Soil Survey shows that the Site�s soil primarily consists of silt-loam, loam, and complexes. The area just south of the warehouse is underlain by Glenville-urban land-Udorthents complex, which indicates possible presence of fill. The Site location and the boundaries of the investigation are included in the Field Sampling Plan, provided as SOW Attachment 1. TASKS TO BE PERFORMED: The Contractor must be a Maryland licensed driller and shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State and local requirements as well as applicable Volpe Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs, see SOW Attachment VII). Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirement. A schedule for these tasks is provided in Section 4. a) Work Plan The Contractor shall attend a kickoff meeting with Volpe Center representatives within five (5) business days of the contract award. During the meeting, Contractor tasks and schedules will be discussed. Prior to the meeting, the contractor shall thoroughly review any Government-furnished information provided to them. Within ten (10) business days of the kickoff meeting, the Contractor shall submit the following in writing to the Volpe Center as part of a brief Work Plan: A description of Contractor�s approach to the tasks as outlined in the following subsections, including the personnel, machinery, and other equipment that is planned to be used. Due to terrain and vegetation conditions at the site, the government prefers that the smallest equipment capable of completing the tasks be used. The Contractor is responsible for the security of equipment staged onsite, if applicable. A proposed schedule of the remaining Contractor tasks as outlined in the following subsections. A description of any required permits needed to perform the work. The Contractor shall be responsible for identifying and obtaining those permits. Copies of the permits shall be submitted to the Volpe Center prior to the start of Site work. If no permits are required, justification for this should be cited. Site Safety and Health Plan, which shall include personnel health and safety precautions to be followed and a Risk Management Plan that identifies major risks and hazards the site and discusses ways to minimize these risks. The Volpe Center will review the Work Plan within five (5) business days of receipt and submit any necessary revisions before approving. If revisions are needed, a revised Work Plan should be returned to the Volpe Center within five (5 business days) of receiving comments. b) Sample Location Access and Vegetation Clearing Some sample (test pit or soil boring) locations are in a wooded area where vegetation and uneven terrain need to be navigated. The Contractor shall clear vegetation and be prepared to access all proposed locations for the geophysical survey, test pitting, and/or soil boring activities described in the following tasks. Volpe visited all sample locations in August 2026 to assess vegetation conditions. At some locations, weeds and grasses up to approximately knee-height, fallen logs up 6 to 12 inches in diameter, and overhead vines and branches were encountered. The contractor shall be prepared to clear vegetation to the extent that equipment can access each sample location from the parking lot and that there is sufficient space to operate the equipment. Based on the conditions observed by Volpe at the site, vegetation is anticipated to be able to be removed by suggested methods such as chainsaw, clippers, weed trimmer, mini-excavator, and hand-removal. No removal of established trees or grading is expected to be needed. Cut materials may be left onsite. Photos of the vegetation conditions observed in August 2026 are included as SOW Attachment 3. During this visit, sample locations were marked with GPS (and may vary from the Field Sampling Plan figures). A PDF file of these field-marked locations is included as SOW Attachment X. c) Geophysical Survey The Contractor shall conduct a geophysical survey to identify potential buried debris stemming from historical automotive junking operations at the Site. The geophysical survey shall be completed by a person qualified and experienced in geophysical surveying and shall incorporate the use of appropriate geophysical sensing equipment (e.g., electromagnetic conductivity, ground penetrating radar, and/or magnetometry) to detect potential buried debris and identify its anticipated depth and extent. The survey will be conducted in approximately 25 ft. x 25 ft. areas centered around each of the six proposed test pit areas, which are targeted to areas with observed surface and/or partially buried debris. These areas are subject to relocation based on site conditions. Within 10 days of completing the survey, the Contractor shall prepare and submit a brief geophysical survey report that shall include a summary of the work performed and equipment used, a description of the findings, a map of surveyed areas and identified anomalies, and photographs of the surveyed areas. d) Utility Clearance The Contractor shall notify Call-Before-You-Dig (811) services in sufficient time before the commencement of soil boring or test pitting activities. The Contractor shall follow all applicable laws to complete this notification. A copy of the notification ticket shall be submitted to the Volpe Center prior to beginning the following tasks. In addition to Call-Before-You-Dig notification, the Contractor shall utilize ground penetrating radar and electromagnetic technologies (or equivalent equipment) to verify Call-Before-You-Dig markings and to complete a private utility locate to clear each of the six proposed test pit locations and ten proposed soil boring locations. If obstructions are present that require a proposed test pit or soil boring to be moved, the Volpe Center will work with a Contractor to identify and clear an alternate location. This task should coincide with the geophysical survey. The locations of the proposed test pits and soil borings are included in

title: RFI - DCSA Personnel Security Alert Management (PSAM) Platform
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Personnel Security Alert Management (PSAM) Platform Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) RFI Reference: DCSA-PSAM-RFI-2026-001 Response Instructions: Due Date: September 22, 2026 @ 1:00pm ET Vendors shall fill out the attached questionnaire and submit it via email to Lindsay Weindruch: lindsay.a.weindruch.civ@mail.mil Disclaimer: This RFI is for informational and planning purposes only. It is not a Request for Proposal, does not commit the Government to any award, and responses are not offers the Government can accept to form a contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted. Do not include classified information in responses; proprietary information will be protected to the extent permitted by law. 1. Purpose DCSA seeks information from Security Information Event Management (SIEM) and Security Operations Center (SOC) platform vendors on commercial capabilities that can support personnel-security operations through cybersecurity event correlation, alert triage, risk-based prioritization, and workflow automation. DCSA is particularly interested in solutions that can identify, correlate, prioritize, and route cybersecurity alerts and incidents associated with members of the trusted workforce for appropriate personnel-security review. 2. Problem Statement DCSA's Continuous Vetting (CV) program faces high daily detection volumes from many sources, much of it low-value noise. Alerts which are drawn from dozens of criminal, financial, terrorism-screening, foreign-contact, foreign-travel, and public-record data sources are still worked largely first-in-first-out rather than by risk, so high-consequence alerts can wait behind routine, low-risk items and case queues have grown faster than staffing. While CV has made progress in detecting potential risk indicators far faster than legacy periodic-reinvestigation models, it is still triaging risk with case-management approaches built for a lower-volume era. 3. Desired Capability DCSA seeks a solution that will incorporate the following capabilities: Ingests and normalizes 40+ structured and unstructured data sources�including APIs, databases, PDFs, and open-source information�into a unified alert stream. Correlates alerts to individual subjects using privacy-preserving tokenization, enabling cross-source analysis without unnecessary exposure of personal data. Applies explainable AI/ML risk scoring aligned with federal adjudicative guidelines�such as financial considerations, criminal conduct, and foreign influence�rather than generic threat categories. Analyst-facing outputs must provide clear rationale (for example, LIME, SHAP, or an equivalent method). Automates low-value alert handling through configurable business rules that suppress duplicates, auto-clear qualifying low-risk alerts, and reduce false positives. Routes alerts through tiered, human-in-the-loop workflows for validation, investigation, and adjudication. The system must prioritize alerts by assessed risk�not age�and immediately escalate critical or high-risk alerts. Supports continuous improvement by feeding adjudicator outcomes back into the rules engine and AI/ML models, subject to appropriate oversight and validation. Integrates with�not replaces�authoritative case-management systems of record through documented, open-standard APIs, including OpenAPI 3.1 and REST. The capability must generate upstream triage signals rather than create a parallel case-management silo. Provides leadership and operational dashboards showing key performance measures, including time to detect, time to respond, false-positive rate, and backlog by priority, with near-real-time visibility into detection, response, and workload status. Avoids vendor lock-in. Proprietary data formats or closed APIs are disqualifying. Can operate in controlled IL5 and classified IL6 environments appropriate for intelligence-derived derogatory information and consistent with Department of War cross-domain security requirements.

description: This combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format at RFO 12.202, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. These analyzers are needed by expeditionary teams for rapid, on-site environmental assessments and baseline surveys in remote areas, reducing the time and costs associated with sample transport and off-site laboratory analysis. The Sci-Aps X-555 Geo-Chem Analyzer is required with the following specifications: The contractor shall provide nine (9) Sci-Aps X-555 Geo-Chem Analyzers. Each analyzer shall be configured to analyze the following elements: Light Rare Earth Elements (REEs): La, Ce, Pr, Nd, and Sm. Heavy REEs: Eu and Gd. Heavy REE Pathfinder: Y. Other Elements: Mg, Al, Si, P, S, K, Ca, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn, As, Se, Rb, Sr, Zr, Nb, Mo, Ta, W, Hg, Pb, Bi, Ag, Cd, Sn, Sb, Cs, and Ba. Each system shall include: Two (2) Li-ion batteries. One (1) battery charger. One (1) ruggedized carrying case. Spare Prolene windows. One (1) operations manual. The Statement of Work (SOW) requires support for all active systems, including previously purchased licenses that are out of maintenance. Confirm the number of existing licenses and whether this quote covers them. ANSWER: The previously purchased site licenses are already covered under a service agreement previously awarded. The OEM requires these new licenses to have their own support agreement for the first year as part of this requirement. The SOW says the work involves PHI and requires a Business Area Agreement (BAA), but the referenced BAA is missing. Confirm expected PHI access and review the BAA before acceptance. Does the VA provide the BAA or are you asking if the vendor has one to provide? ANSWER: Because the support assistance calls will occur with local maintenance personnel accessing the system on a live phone call, there was no PHI access issue. Therefore, the PHI and BAA requirements were deleted from the announcement. The SOW requires an operational tool �free of errors,� resolution of reported defects, and error-free operation access across all clinics. Can the VA confirm these obligations are limited to Apryse�s standard warranty and support commitments? ANSWER: The licenses are for software that is expected to be fully functional upon initial install. However, defect reports and resolutions, version updates, and other software changes are expected to require support from the OEM during warranty term and under the support agreement. As an authorized vendor, you are not expected to provide any error/defect resolution that is under warranty by the OEM, or for future issues/updates covered by the support agreement. The SOW begins September 1, before the quote deadline. Can the VA replace this with a prospective start date tied to award, delivery or activation? ANSWER: The date should have been updated in the SOW to adjust for the RFQ publication. The new version has updated these dates accordingly. Can the VA clarify if option years are needed? It conflicts with the quote SKUs and the SOW. ANSWER: The option year clause should have been removed prior to publication. The six-month service extension is standard to allow additional performance time if needed for some unforeseen reason. This updated RFQ version has the option year clause deleted.

The HESCO MIL 10 is a multi-cellular, geotextile-lined welded mesh barrier system. It is shipped flat-packed on pallets and can be mechanically pulled open and filled with locally sourced materials (earth, sand, gravel, or crushed rock) using standard engineering equipment (such as a front-end loader). SPECIFICATIONS: � Unit Configuration: Multi-cellular, accordion/flat-pack design connected via heavy-duty helical/spiral jointing pins, allowing rapid mechanical deployment and filling via standard engineering equipment (front-end loader/excavator). � Nominal Dimensions (Expanded per Unit): - Height: Approximately 2.21 meters (7 ft 3 in) - Width: Approximately 1.52 meters (5 ft 0 in) - Length: Approximately 30.5 meters (100 ft 0 in) � Wire Mesh Construction: Welded wire mesh manufactured from high-tensile steel wire with a nominal thickness between 4.0 mm and 4.88 mm (6 to 8 Gauge). � Mesh Aperture/Grid: Nominal 76.2 mm x 76.2 mm (3 in x 3 in) spacing. � Corrosion Protection: Steel wire must be coated with Galfan (Zinc-Aluminum alloy) or Hot-Dipped Galvanized to withstand severe outdoor and maritime exposure without structural degradation. � Geotextile Liner: Heavy-duty, UV-stabilized, permeable, non-woven polypropylene geotextile fabric (minimum 250 g/m� weight) designed to retain earth/sand/gravel fill while permitting natural water drainage. � Color Options: Standard Military Tan/Beige or Olive Drab Green. � Logistical Packaging: Units must be shipped fully assembled, compressed, flat-packed on standard commercial/military-compatible pallets, and banded to prevent shifting during multimodal transport. title: 6515--Notice of Intent to Sole Source | Polysomnography System
description: In accordance with FAR 13.106-1(b)/8.405-6(a)(2), this Notice of Intent is to inform all parties the Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 19 located at 6162 South Willow Drive Suite 300, Greenwood Village, CO 80111 intends to award a sole source procurement for the following requirement to the large business manufacturer, Cadwell, located at 909 North Kellogg Street, Kennewick, WA 99336: ITEM # DESCRIPTION OF SERVICE QUANTITY UNIT OF ISSUE 0001 Cadwell Easy III PSG System Period of Performance: 9/30/2026 9/29/2027 4 EA The Fort Harrison VA Sleep Lab requires the replacement of the current polysomnography system that is discontinued and no longer supported. Replacement with the Cadwell III PSG system including amplifiers, cameras, acquisition workstations, scoring software, HL7 interfaces, installation, and training is required. Single-Source Justification Authority: FAR 6.302-1 Only One Responsible Source. 1. Basis for Single-Source Selection (Cadwell Industries, Inc.) Cadwell s Easy III PSG system is the only commercially available sleep system that meets all VA-defined salient characteristics, validated workflows, and network/security constraints documented in the Sleep Lab Deployment Guide v3.2. Cadwell Industries, Inc., (manufacturer) and Cadwell Laboratories, Inc. (serviceprovider) are collectively known as "Cadwell". Cadwell is the only authorized service provider of Cadwell products, including the Easy III PSG. As the manufacturer, and sole service provider, Cadwell trains and equips Technicians to perform all maintenance and repairs required for our products. There are no other entities in the United States that are authorized to provide service for Cadwell products. No other entities maintain technical support personnel who are regularly trained to service and maintain Cadwell products in accordance with our specifications. A. Proprietary amplifier design: The Easy III amplifier provides proprietary physiological channel integration, deterministic DSCP traffic behavior, and VA-approved firmware. B. HL7 workflow compatibility: Cadwell is the only vendor validated for HL7 V2.x MLLP messaging to the Compass Router (10.157.17.38) and VA-standard routing workflows. C. Infrastructure compatibility: Cadwell matches prior VISN deployments and requires no new training, security review, or workflow changes. D. Security and hardening: Cadwell is the only vendor that provided complete Defender exclusions, patch cycles, and hardening documentation. E. Salient characteristics compliance: Only Cadwell met all required signal channels, A/V sync, latency, VLAN/QoS requirements, and export format standards. 2. Summary of Market Research Findings: Four vendors were evaluated. Only Cadwell met 100% of mandatory requirements. Other vendors lacked validated HL7 workflows, proper QoS handling, or security documentation. 3. Impact of Not Using Cadwell: Attempting competition would delay deployment 12 18 months, increase costs, and introduce cybersecurity risk. 4. Fair and Reasonable Price: Pricing aligns with prior VISN purchases and historical benchmarks. Conclusion: Based on technical requirements, interoperability, security needs, and market research, Cadwell is the only responsible source capable of providing a compliant PSG system for the Fort Harrison VA Sleep Lab. FAR 6.302-1 single-source procurement is justified. The associated North America Classification Systems (NAICS) Code is 339112 and the Business Size Standard is 1,000 Employees. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. Interested parties may identify their interest and capability to respond to this requirement no later than 12:00 PM Local Mountain Time, Tuesday, September 22nd, 2026. Information received in response to this notice must clearly demonstrate the capability of meeting the Government s need as stated above. Include any relevant information (specifications, cut sheets, brochures, capability statement, etc.) confirming the ability to supply the products and/or any services outlined in this notice. Responses to this notice are to be sent to barron.long@va.gov. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government is not responsible for any potential costs incurred from interested parties desiring to respond to this notice.

description: The purpose of this RFQ is to solicit quotes for Shure ANX4 Incremental Channel Expansion Licenses and UniFi Indoor Cat6A CMP cable for FEMA Region VI Federal Regional Center and the Texas Room located in the Russell Newman Building. This is an open market RFQ under NAICS 541519, Other Computer Related Services, Information Technology Value Added Resellers, with a size standard of 150 employees. Award will be made on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. All licenses must be valid OEM or publisher-authorized entitlements. All cable supplies must be new, genuine OEM products. Quoters shall provide an itemized quote for each CLIN, including product description, manufacturer, part number, quantity, unit price, extended price, and warranty or license support information. Questions must be emailed to Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov by 12:00 PM CT on September 16, 2026. Quoters must reference RFQ 70FBR626Q00000041 in all correspondence. Phone calls will not be accepted. Quotes must be emailed to Destiny.Dyson@fema.dhs.gov by 1:00 PM CT on September 22, 2026. Late quotes may not be considered. Delivery shall occur within 65 calendar days after receipt of order. Invoices may be submitted only after all required items and license/support information have been delivered and accepted by the Government. The nonmanufacturer rule is not separately stated in the RFQ. The Government confirms that the nonmanufacturer rule does not apply to this acquisition because the RFQ is at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold. All other terms and conditions of the RFQ remain unchanged, including the requirements for new, genuine OEM products and valid publisher-authorized license entitlements, authorized reseller or distributor documentation, delivery, warranty/support, and all applicable RFQ requirements. A non-TAA country of origin, by itself, will not make a CLIN technically unacceptable, provided the quoted item otherwise meets all RFQ requirements, including requirements for new, genuine, authorized, non-counterfeit, non-gray-market products and valid license entitlements. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Fourier Transform Infrared System - PerkinElmer U.S. LLC
description: The Commander, Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC) Procurement Group, Patuxent River, MD 20670 hereby gives notice of their intent to award a purchase order to PerkinElmer U.S. LLC, 710 Bridgeport AVE, Shelton, CT 06484-4797 (CAGE: 9G526) on a sole source basis in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.102(a), only one source reasonably available and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The Materials Engineering Division (MED) at Fleet Readiness Center Southeast (FRCSE) has a requirement to procure a highly specialized, portable, and fully integrated Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) system. Fourier Transform � Infrared Spectroscopy is a critical characterization technique used to obtain infrared spectra of small molecules, polymeric, and composite materials in liquid and solid phases. The existing legacy spectrometer is aged and commercially obsolete, with ongoing system deterioration and the lack of manufacturer support preclude the MED�s ability to guarantee the accuracy and reliability of critical analytical results. Securing a replacement system is paramount, as this instrument is a mission-essential tool required to conduct urgent, point-of-need chemical analysis and material identification directly on the floor of the Aviation Composites Repair facility. The operational environment is characterized by the presence of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and suspended conductive particulates generated during composite repair and painting/coating operations. Due to the significant risk of electrical arcing and ignition in these spaces, an instrument with a low-voltage optical design is mandatory to comply with Navy Safety and Occupational Health (SOH) program guidelines. The primary objective for a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) procurement of one complete, turnkey, portable Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectrometer system utilizing a low voltage laser design. The system must possess specific salient safety and operational characteristics to allow for safe operation within a hazardous industrial environment. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which, if received within four (4) calendar days after the date of the publication of this synopsis, will be considered. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses received as a result of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Point of contact for this requirement is Massoud Koleini at massoud.m.koleini.mil@us.navy.mil.

title: The Data COUNTS� (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times)
description: Description This is a Request for Information (RFI). This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or questions. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain knowledge and information for project planning purposes. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of the RFI or otherwise pay for the information requested. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. The NIH seeks information on technologies and capabilities to further the objectives of the Data COUNTS program. The Data COUNTS� (Collect Data Once, Use Numerous Times) effort is built on collaboration between patients and advocates, government, health systems, technology companies, and the private sector. The Data COUNTS program enables the NIH�s Real-World Data initiative and will provide high quality, standardized data that is provenanced and available through approved access to the research community. The contemplated capability will initially perform requested and approved extraction from Healthcare Partner EMR systems and should be modular and extensible to other authorized source systems such as laboratory information systems, pharmacy information systems, picture archiving and communication systems, vendor-neutral archives, and specialty systems. The Data COUNTS program requires that source data, and source provenance metadata, permissions, and source ontology fields will be preserved without modification or loss. This program will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Technical Requirements of Interest: Address availability and technologies that enable the following features: A durable, Healthcare Partner Leave Behind Technology capability that remains at the Healthcare Partner site after contract completion and can be operated by trained staff without ongoing involvement. The technology should be available and free for use by Healthcare Partners while in the Data COUNTS program. Describe any installation and configuration documentation, operational runbooks, site-controlled credential-transfer procedures, documented dependencies, major-release update procedures, and training that enable independent site operations. Deep query for approved extraction from Healthcare Partner electronic medical records (EMR) systems and other authorized source systems. Capture timestamps and provenance for all data at extraction and maintain an immutable provenance chain. The architecture consumes a machine-readable, version-controlled, authorized, and approved Data Request Specification defining cohort logic, requested source systems, data domains and fields, date range, full or incremental extraction mode, refresh cadence, and applicable authorization and permission rules. Describe how the solution validates data availability against the specification, identifies unavailable or ambiguous fields, avoids silent substitutions, associates the request identifier with each batch and output, and supports reproducible reruns when source data have not changed. An initial automated data quality check validating completeness, uniqueness, data types, date sequencing, and records-per-patient. All anomalies must be reported before any permitted corrections are applied. Sourced data will not be modified De-identification per 45 CFR �164.514(b): remove all 18 direct identifiers; document a consistent de-identification pathway; and apply a per-patient date-shifting specification that preserves temporal order. Privacy Preserving Record Linkage (PPRL) tokenization capabilities for cross-site linkage using an approved, on-premises within the institutional trust boundary PPRL platform that generates consistent, irreversible patient tokens. Describe validation and Healthcare Partner approval before the first live transmission. Describe how token consistency is achieved across independently deployed, site-local PPRL instances, without introducing a shared trust boundary outside the Healthcare Partner site. Describe how the solution preserves all source provenance metadata, permissions information, and ontology fields (e.g. SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10, RxNorm, UCUM, etc.) without modification or loss, excluding authorized de-identification transformations performed under Section 4. The DSP will not create or standardize ontology mappings. Metadata must be additive, clearly identified, and each output value must be traceable to the source and authorized transformation. Describe how the solution consumes authoritative eligibility supplied by the Healthcare Partner and applies it before transmission; records the governing authorization or permission version for each dataset; distinguish cohort exclusions from permission exclusions; and apply revocations so that revoked records are absent from all subsequent refreshes. Describe how the solution generates full and incremental extracts; maintains stable patient tokens; creates unique snapshot and refresh IDs; supports idempotent reruns; identifies added, updated, deleted, merged, unmerged, corrected, and late-arriving records to the appropriate refresh cycle. Workflow Integrity & Processing Audit: maintain audit records for each stage; timestamp, stage ID, batch ID, record counts, outcome, and reconciliation status. Failed reconciliations or incomplete processing stages must halt transmission until resolved or authorized for reprocessing. Security Posture: Describe the ability to attest to HIPAA Security Rule compliance as a Business Associate; Security Audit Logging to generate SIEM-compatible security logs for authentication, administrative actions, configuration changes, and security events. Record timestamp, user/service account, action, resource, and outcome. Security logs must be protected against unauthorized modification or deletion, and logging must be continuous. Defense-in-Depth Encryption: TLS 1.3 where supported; TLS 1.2 minimum for all data in transit,; application-level encryption of output files and VM-level encryption. Attack Surface Minimization with no unnecessary ports, services, or network listeners by default. The only authorized external connection is the outbound TLS path to the Data COUNT Program Also see Section 1 regarding on-site operation of Leave Behind Technology; this section addresses the boundary for identifiable data processing. Describe how identifiable processing is confined to the Healthcare Partner�s VM and institutional trust boundary; only de-identified, tokenized output is transmitted for the Data COUNTS program; access is integrated with Healthcare Partner identity and access controls and is site-managed and logged; and the deployed solution does not include or permit contractor credentials, contractor remote-access pathways, or contractor remote-management capabilities. Describe supported performance at baseline, 2X, and 5X expected workloads and identify assumed data volumes, throughput, processing time, and Healthcare Partner CPU, memory, storage, network and staffing requirements. Describe how the solution can reliably package, transmit, reconcile, and retry deliveries to the TDB, including package, schema versioning, and error resolution. Business Information Requested Please provide information on the following: Details on which capabilities are able to be met Clarification on which features are commercial off-the-shelf (COTS), and which features would be considered minor modifications, and which features would be considered custom development features Billing model and pricing structure and any additional features and their subsequent costs Experience with successful implementation capabilities and list of healthcare partners Experience of similar work with Federal Government agencies Experience of similar work with industries or non-profit organizations Business size and status Response Format: Responses must be submitted by October 1, 2026, 3:00 Eastern Standard Time to DataCounts@nih.gov with the subject line Company Name RFI Response. Responses must be submitted in PDF o

title: Occupational Medical Services (OMS)
description: 1. Purpose The NIH, on behalf of the ORS Division of Occupational Health and Safety, is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of performing Occupational Medical Services and to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether the requirement can be set aside for small business concerns under a socioeconomic program. This notice specifically seeks to determine the availability and capability of: Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) HUBZone Small Businesses Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSB) / Economically Disadvantaged WOSB (EDWOSB) Other small business concerns The Government will use responses to this notice to make decisions regarding set-aside determinations consistent with applicable regulations and Department policy. No award will be made from this notice. 2. Background NIH DOHS operates an Occupational Medical Service that provides work-related medical care and counseling to the NIH workforce, including emergency medical care, pre-placement medical evaluations, medical care for occupational injuries and illnesses, work-related immunizations and health surveillance programs, and employee assistance/counseling services. Performance supports a biomedical research community with potential chemical, biological, animal, physical, and radiological workplace hazards in addition to typical occupational hazards. This is a follow-on to an existing requirement. The Government is considering a single-award, cost-reimbursement (cost-plus-fixed-fee) contract with a base period and option periods, subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS). 3. Anticipated Scope of Work (Summary) The Contractor would be expected to furnish qualified personnel, materials, equipment, and services to perform, at a minimum: Emergency and urgent medical care for work-related conditions Pre-placement and periodic medical evaluations Work-related immunizations and travel medicine Medical surveillance programs (e.g., animal exposure, respiratory/asbestos, TB, hearing conservation, and related biomedical-hazard programs) Employee Assistance Program (EAP) counseling services Clinical operations across multiple fixed sites, with a limited mobile/traveling component (e.g., seasonal flu clinics) Associated quality control/quality improvement, reporting, records management, and information-security/privacy compliance (moderate-impact PII/IT security) Anticipated performance locations include: Bethesda, MD; Frederick, MD; Baltimore, MD; Research Triangle Park, NC; and Hamilton, MT. (Respondents should indicate ability to staff all locations.) 4. Information Requested from Respondents Interested firms are requested to submit a capability statement, not to exceed [8�10] pages, addressing the items below. Marketing materials alone are not sufficient. A. Company Information Company name, UEI/SAM registration status, address, and point of contact (name, title, phone, email). Business size under NAICS 621498 (small or other than small). B. Socioeconomic Status - See Attachment 2. C. Capability and Experience A description of your firm's experience providing occupational medical, ambulatory/clinical, or comparable health services of similar size, scope, and complexity, preferably within the last five (5) years. For up to three (3) relevant contracts, provide: customer/agency, contract number, dollar value, period of performance, contract type, a brief scope description, and whether performed as prime or subcontractor. Experience providing services across multiple geographic locations concurrently. Experience with cost-reimbursement (CPFF) contracts, including whether your firm has an accounting system that has been determined adequate for cost-reimbursement contracts (e.g., by DCAA or a cognizant Federal agency), and the date/type of any such determination. Ability to recruit, credential, and retain licensed clinical staff (e.g., physicians, nurses, PAs, EAP counselors) for federal occupational health work. D. Small Business Participation If your firm is a small business, describe your ability to perform the primary and vital requirements of this effort and to comply with the applicable limitations on subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14) for a set-aside of this type. title: Wash Rack Utility Connection
description: See attachments for full details. The objective of this project is to extend and install necessary electrical power and plumbing (water supply) from the existing Aerospace Ground Equipment (AGE) Shop to the designated exterior Wash Rack. Instructions, Conditions, & Notices to Offerors or Quoters a) The contract provision pertinent to this section is RFO 52.212-1, which has been incorporated by reference. b) Submission of Proposals. Offers shall be submitted no later than 1:00 PM Mountain Standard Time, Tuesday, 22 September 2026 via email to the Contracting Officer, Mr. Joaquin Camacho at joaquin.camacho.3@us.af.mil. All proposals submitted after the deadline will be considered untimely and ineligible for award. c) PROVIDE THE FOLLOWING CONTRACTOR INFORMATION WITHIN YOUR PROPOSAL: Contractor Name: SAM UEI: CAGE Code: Payment Terms (NET 30) or Discount: Point of Contact Name and Phone Number: Email address: Date Offer Expires: Warranty Information: d) Proposals shall be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer identified in Section (b), Submission of Offers. Electronic documents shall be submitted in .pdf, .doc, or .xls and less than 30MB. Communication containing documents in any other format may be blocked or stripped by the Government's server and may not be received by this office. Files in .zip format may not be received by this office. e) To ensure timely and equitable evaluation of offers, offerors must follow the instructions contained herein. The proposal shall be clear, concise and include sufficient detail for effective evaluation. Responses to this solicitation shall strictly adhere to the requirements set forth in the solicitation and the corresponding Statement of Work (SOW). The proposals shall not contain any extraneous information such as advertisements, or marketing information. Offerors must clearly identify any exception(s) taken to the solicitation terms and conditions and provide complete accompanying rationale. Submissions that do not adhere to format and content requirements may be considered non-compliant. The Government reserves the right to eliminate any such quotes from consideration for award. f) Factors 1. Technical Acceptability - The offeror must submit a brief technical execution plan (maximum 2 pages) containing a brief execution narrative. Explicitly demonstrate a logical method to safely trench and connect the electrical and plumbing utilities from the existing Shop to the designated Wash Rack based on the requirements mentioned in the Statement of Work (SOW). Demonstrates a clear and realistic schedule showing project completion within the required 100-day Period of Performance (PoP). 2. Past Performance - The Contracting Officer will evaluate past performance using only Government-maintained records and databases. No past performance references, questionnaires, or client lists are required from the offeror. Databases queried will include the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System (CPARS), SAM.gov (including FAPIIS / Exclusions), and local Contracting Squadron records in accordance with RFO 12.203(a)(2). The Government reserves the right to utilize past performance information obtained from any other readily available official sources of which it is aware. This factor is rated as "Acceptable" when the queried databases indicate a history of successful contract execution, timely performance, and adherence to safety and code standards. An offeror with no record of relevant past performance, or for whom information on past performance is not available, will receive a rating of "Neutral," which shall be graded as "Acceptable" and will not bar the offeror from award. 3. Price (Lowest Evaluated Price) - The offeror must submit a single, lump-sum Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) for CLIN 0001 on their quote sheet (or block 23 of the SF 1449). Price will be evaluated for mathematical accuracy and for price reasonableness in accordance with RFO 12.204(a). Reasonableness will be established by comparing competitive quotes received in response to the solicitation. 2. Site Visit Schedule: 2.1 A site visit has been scheduled for Wednesday, 16 September 2026 at 10:00 AM (MST) and all parties will meet at Truman Gate Visitor Center to be sponsored onto base at 9:30 AM (MST). Attendance at the site visit will be limited to no more than two (2) representatives per company. Please submit the names of your attendees and advise if you require base passes to access Kirtland AFB to the below Points of Contact (POCs) by Tuesday, 15 September 2026, 4:00 PM (MST). Please allow extra time to obtain your pass. The Point of Contact (POC) for base access/EAL request is Joaquin Camacho, 377 MSG/PKC Contracting Officer; Email: joaquin.camacho.3@us.af.mil 2.2 If there questions regarding this solicitation, the site visit or if an offeror believes that there is discrepancies and ambiguities with these instructions, contain an error, omission, ambiguities, or are otherwise unsound, the offeror shall immediately notify the POC in writing with supporting rationale no later than 17 September 2026, 5:00 PM (MST). Answers to the questions will be posted on SAM.gov by close of business on 18 September 2026. 2.3 Incurred Expenses: The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred or associated with preparation and submission of a bid in response to this solicitation.

title: Intent to Sole Source- Automated Blood Bank Instrumentation
description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC/PZIBA) intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to QuidelOrtho Sales Company, LLC, located at 9975 Summers Ridge Road, San Diego, California, 92121. This proposed action is for automated blood bank instrumentation, reagents, consumables, and associated support for the 88th Medical Group Laboratory Flight at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB). This requirement is for a fully automated, continuous-access blood bank system integrated with current and future laboratory information systems, including MHS Genesis, together with the associated training, maintenance, repair, and reagent support necessary to maintain uninterrupted blood bank operations. Extensive market research was conducted to identify potential sources. Techniques included, but were not limited to, internet market research, review of similar procurements, input from Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), review of the Government�s minimum technical requirements, and a Sources Sought notice. The BPA justification states that no existing mandatory source has been identified that can satisfy the organization�s specific blood and blood product requirements. The WPAFB 88th Medical Group requires a blood bank instrumentation solution that meets the minimum technical requirements established in the Statement of Work (SOW). These requirements include a fully automated blood bank system using the required methodology, support for required blood bank testing on a single platform, integration capability with MHS Genesis, FDA-approved reagent kits, and instrument-specific reagents, controls, standards, and hardware from the manufacturer producing the instrument. Utilizing a system that does not meet these requirements would not satisfy the Government�s operational and patient care needs. As part of this market research effort, a Sources Sought notice was posted on SAM.gov on 20 August 2026. One response was received. The 88th Medical Group completed a technical evaluation and found the submission technically unacceptable. The evaluations identified deficiencies including wrong methodology and instrumentation, different reagents for the instrumentation, and failure to meet upgrade-of-equipment requirements. The Contracting Officer has determined that only one source is reasonably available: QuidelOrtho Sales Company, LLC. This proposed procurement will be a Sole Source under North American Industry Classification System code (NAICS) 325413 � Blood derivative in-vitro diagnostic substances manufacturing, with a size standard of 1,250 employees. The proposed source is QuidelOrtho Sales Company, LLC., 9975 Summers Ridge Road, San Diego, California, 92121. Submission Instructions and Points of Contact: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties who believe they can satisfy the requirements must provide a capability statement with clear and convincing evidence of their ability to do so. The statement must demonstrate the vendor's capability to provide automated blood bank instrumentation, reagents, consumables, and support services that are fully compatible with the Government�s minimum technical and operational requirements identified in the Statement of Work. A simple statement of capability is not sufficient. All responses, questions, and capability statements shall be submitted via email to the following points of contact no later than 22 September 2026 at 3:00PM EST. � Contract Specialist: Alejandro Quiles, alejandro.quiles_sanchez.1@us.af.mil � Contracting Officer: Claire Hess, claire.hess@us.af.mil All correspondence sent via email must contain the subject line: "Intent to Sole Source- Automated Blood Bank Instrumentation & Support." Be advised that emails without this exact subject line or with prohibited attachments (.zip, .exe) may be blocked by network filters. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals or quotes. A decision by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government.
